study.title: An oral coral-like resveratrol nanocomplex protects against dry eye disease through ocular and systemic redox homeostasis

cover.headline: An oral resveratrol nanocomplex is linked to **protection against dry eye disease** in mice.

slides.title: Dry eye disease involves chronic inflammation and oxidative stress, but topical treatments face compliance issues.
slides.body:
Dry eye disease progressively damages ocular tissues through inflammation and oxidative stress working together. Standard topical treatments like anti-inflammatory drops and artificial tears face poor long-term compliance and side effects.

Emerging evidence suggests systemic oxidative imbalance contributes to the disease. Oral antioxidants could offer a complementary approach, but poor absorption and rapid clearance have limited their use. Resveratrol, a polyphenol antioxidant, faces exactly this bioavailability problem.

slides.title: A coral-like nanocomplex increased resveratrol bioavailability by 6.62-fold and ocular accumulation by 2.49-fold in mice.
slides.body:
Researchers created a coral-like resveratrol nanocomplex using sericin and dipotassium glycyrrhizinate as natural carriers. This formulation markedly enhanced gastrointestinal stability and systemic exposure compared to regular resveratrol.

In mice, oral bioavailability increased approximately 6.62-fold. Ocular accumulation rose 2.49-fold. The nanocomplex was associated with protection against benzalkonium chloride-induced corneal damage, tear film dysfunction, and inflammatory responses in an experimental dry eye model.

slides.title: The nanocomplex was associated with both ocular and systemic redox balance, plus shifts in gut microbiota.
slides.body:
The protective effects appeared to work through both local ocular antioxidant activity and systemic redox homeostasis. Rather than acting solely on the eye surface, the oral formulation may offer complementary benefits through multiple pathways.

The nanocomplex was also associated with modulation of gut microbiota composition and metabolic profiles in the mice. This suggests oral redox intervention could reduce reliance on prolonged topical treatment by addressing systemic factors that contribute to dry eye disease.

caveats: This study found a pattern, not a cause. Other factors could explain the association between the nanocomplex and dry eye protection.
This was done in mice, not humans. Most findings in mice do not translate to people.

cta.headline: Oral antioxidants for eye disease
cta.sub: A bioavailability problem meets nanotechnology in a mouse model of dry eye.

caption: A new resveratrol delivery system is associated with protection against dry eye disease in mice, working through both ocular and systemic antioxidant pathways rather than just topical action. The coral-like nanocomplex used natural carriers—sericin and dipotassium glycyrrhizinate—and was fabricated through a pH-ultrasonic-shifting method in water. Published in Bioactive Materials, the study used mice with experimentally induced dry eye. This was a pattern-finding study in animals, and most mouse findings don't translate to humans. Full study: doi.org/10.1016/j.bioactmat.2026.08.039 Do you use eye drops?
